name: bing_search_chromium
description: Bing web search (organic results). Fixed bing.com host; country routed via cc= and language via setlang= (derived from the locale). Materializer lowercases `country` for cc= and derives a language code for setlang= from the locale. Every organic href is a click-tracking wrapper — bing.com/ck/a?...&u=a1<base64url> — so `links` read straight from href pointed at bing.com on EVERY row: a field 100% populated and 100% useless, which no fill-rate check can see. The destination is recovered by pulling the `u=a1` capture and base64-decoding it. An href that is not a wrapper yields null rather than a mangled value. ENGINE: Chromium (Playwright), stealth off. chromium_webgl_identity()'s host-aligned WebGL claim (an AMD Radeon 780M string under a Windows UA) does NOT apply here: it runs only inside stealth_config(), which src/browser/runner.py:194 reaches only when stealth is on, so this preset ships the browser's raw headless WebGL identity instead. No fingerprint_profile, which the Chromium runner would accept and ignore. MEASURED 2026-08-27 (n=2 per locale, 6 runs per engine, research/preset_audit_dual_engine_2026_08_27.json): 6/6 runs returned data on both engines, 10 rows each on us and ru. On de THIS VARIANT UNDER-COLLECTED — 2 rows and 5 rows, both with row_alignment_mismatch (titles=2/links=2/snippets=1 and titles=5/links=5/snippets=4) — against 10 and 10 for bing_search_camoufox from the same URL with the same selector. Every row it did return is one of the ten rows the twin got from the same German SERP, in the same order — chip.de and pcwelt.de on the 2-row run, those two plus PCMag, Tom's Hardware and Forbes on the 5-row run. ROW-COUNT CAUSE, corrected 2026-08-28 fix round 2 (reproduced in tests/presets/test_bing_search_row_alignment.py): for the two raw captures actually in hand (bing_camoufox_de.html classic, bing_chromium_de.html Copilot -- both complete, well-formed final pages, not truncated mid-render snapshots), it is NOT the wait strategy an earlier read of this audit blamed for those two specific pages -- both twins ship identical wait_until=domcontentloaded / no wait_for_selector / timeout_ms=30000, and this same engine returned a full 10 rows on us and ru in the same run. Bing draws one of two different SERP layouts per session: the classic layout (ten li.b_algo, nothing else) and a Copilot/generative-answer layout that, on the capture in hand, renders 3 li.b_algo AND promotes its rank-1 organic result OUT of the list entirely into div.b_wpt_bl, a card inside the answer widget reusing the exact same title/link/snippet template as li.b_algo (verified: it decoded to the SAME destination, title and snippet as li.b_algo's own rank-1 on the classic capture). A first version of this fix widened the selector for the layout gap but missed this promoted card, undercounting by one on every Copilot draw shaped like the capture in hand. The selector now also matches div.b_wpt_bl h2 a[href*='u=a1'] -- an h2-scoped anchor carrying the organic redirect prefix, not the container class alone -- because the SAME answer widget has three OTHER div.b_wpt_bl siblings (a YouTube card, a topic-filter strip, a Gesponsert ad card) that carry real u=a1- or aclk-shaped hrefs of their own but have no h2 at all, PLUS a constructed regression case proving u=a1 itself is load-bearing rather than redundant with the h2 gate: an ad card whose title anchor DOES sit inside an h2 (a shape Bing's own ad templates already use elsewhere on this same page) is excluded only because its href is a bare aclk redirect, not u=a1. Verified end-to-end with extract_fields against the real captures: a clean 10/10/10/10 on the classic capture and a clean 4/4/4/4 on the Copilot one (rank 1 = the promoted PCMag card, matching the classic capture's own rank 1), zero warnings both times. If a page ever renders BOTH the promoted card AND leaves its own rank-1 result in li.b_algo -- unobserved, but not excludable, see the historical-runs paragraph below -- this preset emits that result twice; co-occurrence is not currently guarded against. Separately, li.b_ans.b_top (Bing's generated-answer prose) is excluded, but not because its anchors are empty -- it holds 22 real anchors decoding to 5 distinct external hosts (forbes.com, pcwelt.de, chip.de, faz.net, produkte-im-test.de), all numbered citation footnotes. Its own three h2's, checked directly, contain zero anchors between them, which is the actual, narrower reason an h2-scoped selector cannot reach them. li.b_ad.b_adBottom's three nested ads (a visible 'Gesponsert' badge, an aclk -- not ck/a -- redirect whose u= value lacks the organic a1 prefix) remain excluded the same way they always were. NOT resolved by this fix, and NOT confirmed to be the same defect: the historical 2-row and 5-row runs (research/preset_audit_dual_engine_2026_08_27.json entries 30-31), including the row_alignment_mismatch itself (titles=2/links=2/snippets=1 and titles=5/links=5/snippets=4 -- always exactly one snippet short). Their raw HTML was never kept (the audit record stores a slimmed row count, not markup), so neither their layout NOR the wait-strategy account of them can be confirmed or ruled out -- and the one piece of entry 31 that CAN be checked argues against assuming it hit the same mechanism as the capture in hand: it was collected under the OLD selector (li.b_algo h2 a[href^='http'], which cannot reach div.b_wpt_bl), yet its own links[0] is https://www.pcmag.com/picks/the-best-laptops -- meaning PCMag was reachable there as an ordinary li.b_algo, not promoted out of the list the way it is on the capture in hand. Entry 31's 5-row, one-snippet-short composition is therefore at least as consistent with a page snapshotted mid-render (5 of 10 classic slots painted so far, CHIP's caption not yet among them) as with any Copilot-layout account of it. Track entries 30-31 as open and their layout as unobserved, not as confirmed instances of the mechanism this fix addresses. Also not asserted: that which layout a session draws correlates with engine. The two raw captures in hand are one Copilot-layout observation on Chromium and one classic-layout observation on Camoufox -- n=1 each. The historical runs' layouts are unobserved (previous paragraph), and entry 31's own composition argues against counting it as a second Chromium/Copilot data point rather than for it. No number is put on any correlation, and no engine preference is asserted for de in either direction. MEASURED 2026-08-28 (retest of the same twenty presets through the same harness after the five audit fixes; n=2 per locale, 92 runs, research/preset_audit_dual_engine_2026_08_28.json): THE COPILOT ROW FIX COULD NOT BE TESTED: Bing did not serve the Copilot layout to any exit on 2026-08-28. A dedicated probe sending this preset's exact request, with the shipped union split into its li.b_algo and div.b_wpt_bl halves, found div.b_wpt_bl container count 0 on 18 of 18 runs (3 runs x 3 locales x both engines); the promoted card was never rendered, so no run in this round exercises the widened branch. It does show the widening is free on the classic layout: shipped rows == li.b_algo rows on 18/18. Audit rows here: 6/5/10/5/2/11 (08-27: 2/5/10/10/10/10) -- the spread is Bing's own, not a wait or selector defect, and the same probe watched a single de exit render 2, 7 and 5 li.b_algo slots on three consecutive requests. TWO THINGS ARE UNCHANGED AND STILL OPEN. (1) The snippet misalignment reproduces at exactly the same rate and shape as 08-27: 2 of 6 runs, both on de, with snippets one short of the other three fields (6/6/5/6 and 5/5/4/5) and row_alignment_mismatch warned. (2) The poisoned SERP is worse, not better: 3 of this variant's 6 runs answered a DIFFERENT query at HTTP 200 -- both ru runs (Pinterest/zhihu threads; 'High Profit Margin Products') and us#1, which returned the bare 'best' SERP (Best Buy, Merriam-Webster) with 11 rows, the HIGHEST count in the whole record set. Row count still tracks poisoning rather than health.

titles.selector: li.b_algo h2 a[href*='&u=a1'], li.b_algo h2 a[href*='?u=a1'], div.b_wpt_bl h2 a[href*='&u=a1'], div.b_wpt_bl h2 a[href*='?u=a1']

links.selector: li.b_algo h2 a[href*='&u=a1'], li.b_algo h2 a[href*='?u=a1'], div.b_wpt_bl h2 a[href*='&u=a1'], div.b_wpt_bl h2 a[href*='?u=a1']

snippets.selector: (//li[contains(concat(' ', normalize-space(@class), ' '), ' b_algo ')] | //div[contains(concat(' ', normalize-space(@class), ' '), ' b_wpt_bl ')][.//h2//a[contains(@href, '&u=a1') or contains(@href, '?u=a1')]])//div[contains(concat(' ', normalize-space(@class), ' '), ' b_caption ')]//p | (//li[contains(concat(' ', normalize-space(@class), ' '), ' b_algo ')] | //div[contains(concat(' ', normalize-space(@class), ' '), ' b_wpt_bl ')][.//h2//a[contains(@href, '&u=a1') or contains(@href, '?u=a1')]])//p[contains(concat(' ', normalize-space(@class), ' '), ' b_lineclamp2 ')]

result_blocks.selector: //li[contains(concat(' ', normalize-space(@class), ' '), ' b_algo ')] | //div[contains(concat(' ', normalize-space(@class), ' '), ' b_wpt_bl ')][.//h2//a[contains(@href, '&u=a1') or contains(@href, '?u=a1')]]
